items.v: Pain in chest
Obstructed breathing
Seizures
Thoughts of harming self or baby
Bleeding, heavy or increasing
Incision not healing
Red or swollen leg
Temperature 100.4 F (38 C) or higher
Headache, severe, or vision change

mnemonics.note: The ACOG standard. The site notes list fainting where ACOG has seizures; same red-flag family. Any one of these means urgent assessment, do not wait for the scheduled visit.
mnemonics.title: POST-BIRTH

items.v: Redness
Edema
Ecchymosis
Drainage
Approximation

mnemonics.note: Assess the repair or incision in side-lying or Sims position. Worsening redness, drainage, or separation is a flag, not expected recovery.
mnemonics.title: REEDA

mnemonics.hook: Lochia changes color as it heals

items.v: Dark red, first few days
Pinkish, around days 3 to 10
Yellow-white, over subsequent weeks

mnemonics.note: Rubra to serosa to alba. Timing varies; assess the whole pattern. Foul lochia or a return to bright red is a warning sign.
mnemonics.title: Red, Pink, Pale

mnemonics.hook: Three things that raise clot risk after birth

items.v: Hypercoagulability: pregnancy makes blood clot more easily
Vessel injury: birth trauma to blood vessels
Immobility: stasis from bed rest or limited movement

mnemonics.note: Pregnancy and birth stack all three. Early movement and watching for a painful swollen leg are the nursing answers.
mnemonics.title: Virchow's Triad

items.v: Methylergonovine: avoid with hypertension or preeclampsia, check BP first
Carboprost: avoid with asthma, check breathing first

mnemonics.note: Both stop postpartum bleeding. The drug choice depends on the patient, not just the bleeding.
mnemonics.title: M is for Pressure, C is for Chest

mnemonics.hook: Rubin's phases of becoming a parent

items.v: Taking-in: early recovery, dependence, retelling the birth story
Taking-hold: learning to care for the baby, seeking guidance
Letting-go: accepting the new role, growing into a parental identity

mnemonics.note: The phases overlap and move at their own pace. Meet physical needs first, then teach when the parent is ready.
mnemonics.title: Taking-in, Taking-hold, Letting-go

items.v: Alone: baby sleeps alone, no bed-sharing
Back: on the back for every sleep
Crib: firm flat surface, empty crib, nothing loose

mnemonics.note: No blankets, pillows, or toys in the sleep space. Every sleep, every time, including naps.
mnemonics.title: ABCs of Safe Sleep

mnemonics.hook: Two scalp swellings, one suture-line rule

items.v: Caput succedaneum crosses suture lines. Soft-tissue swelling, present at birth, gone in days.
Cephalohematoma is confined by suture lines. Blood under the periosteum, appears hours later, gone in weeks.
Subgaleal hemorrhage spreads and can hold a large blood volume. That is the emergency.

mnemonics.note: Crosses or confined is the exam question. Subgaleal is the one that can cause shock.
mnemonics.title: Caput Crosses, Cephalo Confined

mnemonics.hook: The gestational-age staircase, odd numbers up

items.v: Early term (before 37 is preterm)
Full term
Late term
Postterm

mnemonics.note: For size, 10 and 90 are the fences: under the 10th percentile is SGA, over the 90th is LGA, between is AGA.

items.v: Heat lost from wet skin. Dry the baby.
Heat lost to cooler air. Protect from drafts.
Heat lost to cold surfaces. Use warm surfaces.
Heat lost to nearby cold objects. Keep the bassinet away from cold walls and windows.

mnemonics.note: Cold stress raises oxygen and glucose use and can cause acidosis. Warmth is a vital sign in a newborn.
mnemonics.title: Four Ways Babies Lose Heat

mnemonics.hook: Three causes of newborn breathing trouble

items.v: Respiratory distress syndrome: no surfactant, stiff lungs, mostly preterm.
Transient tachypnea: lung fluid not cleared, often term or late preterm, often after cesarean without labor. Improves over days.
Meconium aspiration: meconium breathed in, blocks and inflames airways, often postterm or meconium-stained fluid.

mnemonics.note: Signs overlap, so use birth history and the exam together. RDS is a surfactant problem, TTN is a fluid problem, MAS is a blockage problem.
mnemonics.title: RDS, TTN, MAS

items.v: Diamond-shaped, closes around 18 months
Triangular, closes around 8 to 12 weeks

mnemonics.note: Timing varies. Persistent bulging, marked depression, or unusual head size needs review.
mnemonics.title: Diamond 18, Triangle 8 to 12

mnemonics.hook: Three fetal shunts, in blood-flow order

items.v: Ductus venosus bypasses the liver, sending umbilical blood toward the inferior vena cava.
Foramen ovale bypasses the right-to-left heart circuit, right atrium to left atrium.
Ductus arteriosus bypasses the lungs, pulmonary artery to descending aorta.

mnemonics.note: Each shunt skips one organ. The cord rule: 1 vein in (oxygen-rich), 2 arteries out (oxygen-poor).
mnemonics.title: Liver, Heart, Lungs

items.v: Latch: deep, comfortable, wide mouth
Audible swallow: hear or see swallowing, not just sucking
Type of nipple
Comfort: no persistent pain
Hold: positioning that supports the latch

mnemonics.note: Judge the feed by latch, swallowing, and comfort, not by minutes at the breast. Persistent pain or poor transfer means lactation referral.
mnemonics.title: LATCH

items.v: At room temperature, up to 77 F (25 C)
Refrigerated, up to 40 F (4 C)
Freezer best, up to 12 months acceptable, at 0 F (-18 C)

mnemonics.note: Never microwave milk and never refreeze fully thawed milk. Thaw in the refrigerator or lukewarm water.

items.v: Amenorrhea: no periods since birth
Age under 6 months
All breastmilk: full or nearly full breastfeeding

mnemonics.note: Feeding gaps no longer than 4 hours by day, 6 by night. All three must hold. One fails, LAM fails.
mnemonics.title: LAM and the 3 A's

items.v: Paragard (copper), up to 10 years
Mirena and Liletta, up to 8 years
Kyleena, 5 years
Skyla, 3 years

mnemonics.note: Nexplanon, the implant, is up to 5 years. Document the device, insertion date, and replacement plan.

items.v: Thin homogeneous discharge
Vaginal pH over 4.5
Positive whiff (amine) test
Clue cells on microscopy

mnemonics.note: Three of the four makes the clinical diagnosis. Lab testing can also be used.
mnemonics.title: Amsel: 3 of 4

items.v: Painless, bright-red bleeding, soft nontender uterus. Placenta covers the cervical opening.
Painful, dark-red bleeding, rigid tender uterus. Placenta separates early; blood can hide behind it.

mnemonics.note: No digital vaginal exam before previa is excluded. In abruption, visible bleeding can underestimate severity, and DIC is a risk.
mnemonics.title: Painless Previa, Painful Abruption

mnemonics.hook: Check before you give it and while it runs

items.v: Respirations: rate and effort
Reflexes: deep tendon reflexes
Renal: urine output

mnemonics.note: Toxicity signs: respirations under 12 per minute, urine output under 25 to 30 mL per hour, absent or decreasing reflexes. If any R fails, stop the drip and reach for calcium gluconate.
mnemonics.title: Magnesium and the 3 R's

mnemonics.hook: Two blood pressure lines in preeclampsia

items.v: Preeclampsia starts here: systolic 140 or diastolic 90 or higher, on repeat measures.
Severe: confirm within about 15 minutes, treat within 30 to 60 minutes.

mnemonics.note: Severe features: Head (persistent severe headache), Eyes (visual change), Belly (right-upper-quadrant or epigastric pain). Labs: platelets under 100,000, creatinine over 1.1. Preeclampsia does not require proteinuria.
mnemonics.title: 140/90 Is the Door, 160/110 Is the Alarm

mnemonics.hook: Infections that can reach the fetus

items.v: Toxoplasmosis: cook meat, wash produce, let someone else handle cat litter.
Other, syphilis in these notes: transplacental infection, treat with penicillin.
Rubella: early infection can cause heart, eye, and hearing problems. MMR before pregnancy or postpartum, never during.
CMV: can cause hearing loss and growth or neurologic problems. Test by saliva or urine PCR in the first 21 days.
Herpes simplex: most neonatal infection happens during birth. Active lesions usually mean cesarean.

mnemonics.note: TORCH is a reminder of possible congenital and perinatal infections, not a diagnosis by itself.
mnemonics.title: TORCH

items.v: Fasting
1 hour
2 hours
3 hours

mnemonics.note: 100-gram, 3-hour test. At or above a threshold is abnormal; at least two of the four values are needed for a GDM diagnosis. Screen first with the 50-gram, 1-hour challenge at 24 to 28 weeks.

items.v: Help: call for help, start timing from birth of the head
Evaluate for episiotomy
Legs: McRoberts, thighs sharply flexed toward the abdomen
Lift: suprapubic pressure just above the pubic bone
Enter: internal rotation, the Woods screw
Remove the posterior arm
Roll to all-fours, the Gaskin maneuver

mnemonics.note: Never fundal pressure, never forceful jerking or downward traction on the head. The site notes cover Help, Legs, Pressure, and Enter; the full HELPERR sequence is the clinical standard.
mnemonics.title: HELPERR

mnemonics.hook: Five forces that decide how labor goes

items.v: Bony pelvis and soft tissues, including cervix and vagina
Fetus and placenta: size, flexion, presentation
Contractions thin and dilate the cervix; bearing down moves the baby in the second stage
Maternal position shapes the fit and the progress
Response: fear, support, and coping change the experience and the outcome

mnemonics.note: A pelvis label alone does not guarantee the birth route. All five P's work together.
mnemonics.title: The 5 P's of Labor

mnemonics.hook: Perineal laceration degrees, skin to rectum

items.v: Skin and superficial tissue
Perineal muscles
Anal sphincter
Rectal mucosa

mnemonics.note: The degrees describe injury depth, not a pain scale. Deeper tears need more repair and more recovery support.
mnemonics.title: 1, 2, 3, 4: How Deep?

mnemonics.hook: Four cues of suspected intraamniotic infection

items.v: Maternal fever
Fetal tachycardia
Uterine tenderness
Foul-smelling amniotic fluid

mnemonics.note: Suspected intraamniotic infection means recognize and escalate. Mother and baby both need assessment and the team needs to know.
mnemonics.title: Fever, Fast Heart, Tender Uterus, Foul Fluid

items.v: Soft cervix
Bluish-purple cervix or vaginal tissue, from increased blood flow
Soft lower uterine segment

mnemonics.note: These are probable signs of pregnancy, not proof by themselves. They suggest pregnancy; they do not confirm it.
mnemonics.title: Goodell, Chadwick, Hegar

items.v: The patient's symptoms: missed period, nausea, breast tenderness
Findings that suggest pregnancy: cervical signs, positive pregnancy test
Direct evidence of an embryo or fetus: fetal heartbeat, ultrasound, fetal movement felt by the examiner

mnemonics.note: Only positive signs confirm pregnancy. Presumptive and probable signs point toward it.
mnemonics.title: Presumptive, Probable, Positive
